plastering.guide: Plastering in a lived-in house is mostly making a flat, sound surface that paint and paper will sit on. We skim ceilings and walls, replaster rooms that have blown, run coving and cornice, take Artex off where it is safe to do so, dot-and-dab dry lining, and patch the hole left by a leak or a removed wall light. A full-house plaster is a different job from a patch: the whole room is protected, the old material is cut back to a sound edge, and the new coat is ruled flat. We talk you through bonding coat, hardwall and multi-finish in ordinary words. We do not ask you to choose a brand from a catalogue. The free survey looks at how hollow the old plaster is, whether the ceiling is lath and plaster or board, and how we get boards up the stairs.
paragraphs: Skimming is a thin finish coat over sound plaster or new board. If the background is live, we do not skim over it and hope. We cut the loose material out and dub it back out so the skim has something to hold.
Coving and cornice hide the joint between wall and ceiling and they also crack when the ceiling moves. A repair is a short length let into the old run, not a smear of filler along the whole room.
Artex removal is dusty. We protect the room, check what the texture is stuck to, and skim the ceiling afterwards so you are not left with a scarred board.
Dry lining and dot-and-dab suit walls that are out of true. The boards need a proper fix and the sockets need extending. We do not leave the electrician with a box buried in the dab.
Patch plastering after a leak has to go past the stain, not just over it. We stop when the surrounding plaster is firm. A small patch that flashes through paint is a failed patch.
Lath and plaster ceilings in older {place} houses can be tired. We will say if a board-and-skim replacement is the honest repair rather than another skim on laths that have let go.
Venetian and polished plaster are decorative finishes. They need a flat background and a sample agreed before the room is committed. They are not a way to hide a moving crack.
Full-house plastering is sequenced around the other trades. Joiners, electricians and the decorator all need the plaster hard before they return. We write that order into the quote.

rendering.guide: Rendering is the outside coat on a wall: sand and cement, silicone, monocouche, K-rend, acrylic or a Tyrolean finish. It keeps weather off the masonry and it is also what the street sees. We re-render whole elevations, patch cracks, remove pebble-dash that has let go, and paint render that is sound but tired. A render quote without looking at the substrate is a guess. We check whether the old coat is hollow, whether the wall has had cavity insulation, and where the water is getting in. Pebble-dash removal is noisy and it marks the brick underneath, so we agree the finish before we start. Silicone and monocouche are through-coloured. A patch in those systems has to be planned or it will show.
paragraphs: K-rend and other thin-coat systems need a clean, stable background and the beads and stops the manufacturer expects. We do not trowel a branded name onto dusty old render.
Pebble-dash removal leaves a rough face. The new coat has to be thick enough to hide that, or the brick pattern ghosts through.
Hairline cracks in render are often movement or a bad day-joint. We cut out to a line that can be made good, rather than painting a crack and calling it repaired.
Render and external wall insulation are related but they are not the same visit. If the wall is insulated we do not fix through it without knowing what is behind.
Painting render is only worth doing when the coat is stuck. We tap the elevation first. Hollow render gets cut out.
Sills, bellcasts and the joint with the damp course decide whether the wall sheds water or drinks it. They are on the survey.
A coloured render patch on a {place} semi will show if the batch does not match. We talk about that before you choose a patch over a full elevation.
Scaffold or a safe tower is part of the job on anything above the ground floor. We do not quote a price that pretends the ladders are free.

bricklaying.guide: Bricklaying for a house is garden walls, boundary repairs, repointing, lintels, spalled bricks, chimney rebuilds, brick arches and blockwork. New brickwork has to be tied, level and in the right mortar. Old brickwork in {place} is often soft brick and lime, and a hard cement point drives the damp into the face and the brick spalls. We look at the mortar before we price repointing. A garden wall that leans is not a repoint. It may need rebuilding, and we say which. Lintel replacement means propping. We do not cut a slot under a load and hope. Wall ties and brick arches are separate from a simple point, and they are named if the survey finds them.
paragraphs: Repointing is raked out to a proper depth and packed, not smeared over the old joint. Smear pointing cracks off and looks poor.
Lime mortar suits older soft brick. We use it where the wall was built that way, and we do not default to a bag of strong cement.
Spalled bricks are cut out and matched as closely as the yard allows. A bright new brick in a weathered wall is agreed with you first.
A leaning garden wall is measured. If it is past a safe lean we rebuild it rather than point it and leave the lean.
Chimney rebuilds need roof access and a weather plan. The stack is taken down to sound brick and rebuilt, flaunched and flued as agreed.
Blockwork for an extension or a garage is set out from the drawing, not from a chalk line on the day with no check.
Brick arches over openings sag when the mortar has gone. The repair is propped and rebuilt, not pointed from a ladder in the rain.
Lintels are specified for the span and the load. We do not bed a too-short concrete lintel because it was on the van.

extensions.guide: A house extension is a single storey, a double storey, a rear, a side return, a wrap-around, a kitchen extension, a garage conversion, a porch or an orangery. The building work is the shell, the opening-up, the roof, the floor and the making good. Planning and building regulations are part of the conversation, not a surprise at the end. We survey the garden, the drains, the neighbour's wall and the way into the site. A side return in a terrace is tight. A wrap-around changes the kitchen and the living room together. We write what is in the quote: excavations, brick or block, the roof type, the steel if a wall comes out, and who does the kitchen at the end. We do not hand you a brochure price for 'an extension'.
paragraphs: Single-storey rear extensions are the common job. The drain run under the new floor is found before we dig, not after the concrete is in.
Double-storey work needs a proper design for the foundations and the joint with the existing roof. We will not start from a sketch on a napkin.
Side-return extensions steal the side alley. We check headroom, the neighbour's gutter and how materials get to the back.
Garage conversions fail when the floor is too low, the walls are single skin and the roof is a flimsy asbestos or felt lid. We say so on the survey.
A porch is small and still needs a damp course, a roof that does not dump water on the step, and a door that actually fits.
Steels for a knock-through are calculated and the padstones are sized. We do not bed a beam on a single brick and call it done.
The quote separates shell from fit-out when you want it that way, so the kitchen and the plaster are not hidden inside one vague line.
Neighbours get told before the digger arrives. Party-wall matters are flagged. We do not pretend they are optional on a terrace.

loft-conversions.guide: A loft conversion is a dormer, a hip-to-gable, a mansard, a Velux room-in-the-roof, or the simpler boarding and ladder that makes the loft usable without calling it a bedroom. The structure is the job: joists that were not designed for a bedroom, the stairs, the fire door, the insulation and the way out. We survey the loft, the landing and the roof pitch before we talk about a dormer. A hip-to-gable changes the outside of the house and the neighbour's view of the roof. A Velux conversion keeps the roofline and only works if the headroom is already there. Boarding and a ladder are honest jobs when a full conversion is more than you need. We do not sell you a bedroom that fails the headroom.
paragraphs: Dormers need a structural opening in the roof and a proper cheek and roof. We do not bolt a timber box to rafters and hope.
Hip-to-gable conversions change the gable wall. Party-wall and the tile match are discussed before the scaffold goes up.
Mansards are heavier and less common on ordinary semis. If the roof is not suitable we say so.
Velux loft rooms live or die on headroom and the stair. We measure both on the survey.
Loft boarding for storage is not a conversion. We still check the joists before we load them with board and boxes.
A loft ladder has to land somewhere safe on the landing. We do not cut a hole over the stairwell.
Insulation and ventilation stop the new room sweating. They are in the quote, not an extra on the last day.
Fire separation and the stair enclosure are explained in plain words. A bedroom in the loft without a proper way down is not finished.

It is also the moment the plumber and the electrician have to be in the right order. We fit kitchens you have bought and we refit tired ones: new doors, a new worktop, a tiled splashback. A full installation includes levelling the units, scribing to uneven walls, and connecting the appliances we agreed. We do not plumb gas ourselves as if we were the Gas Safe engineer. Gas work is carried out by Gas Safe registered engineers. The free survey in {place} checks the walls, the floor, the waste and whether the consumer unit can take the oven and the hob.

Plumbing for a sink or a dishwasher is part of the fit when it is on the quote. We test the waste before we push the unit back.
End panels, cornice and pelmet are the bits that make a kitchen look finished. They are listed, not forgotten.
We protect floors and we take the old kitchen away if that was agreed. A hallway full of old units is not a finished job.
Landlords refitting between tenancies need a date. We book the electrician and the decorator around that date rather than leaving you to chase three people.

bathrooms.guide: Bathroom fitting covers a full refit, a bath swap, an en-suite, a wet room, a walk-in shower and a disabled adaptation. Water, waste, ventilation and the tray or the bath have to agree with each other. We strip out, move wastes where the joists allow, board and tank wet areas, and fit the suite you chose. Electric showers are an electrical job as well as a plumbing one, and they are on the quote when you want one. We do not use a CCTV photograph or a plastering photograph to show a bathroom. The survey looks at the floor, the stack, the fan and whether the ceiling below is someone's living room. A wet room needs a fall and a drain. A walk-in shower needs a tray that does not rock.
paragraphs: Wet rooms fail at the tanking and the fall, not at the tiles. We get the floor right before anyone picks a tile.
A bath replacement in a {place} terrace often means a door that is narrower than the bath. We measure the route in, not just the room.
En-suites stolen from a bedroom need a waste that can fall to the stack. If it cannot, we say so before the stud wall goes up.
Walk-in showers need a solid tray, a screen that meets the tray, and a fan that actually extracts.
Disabled adaptations are about the person who will use the room: rails, the shower seat, the door swing. We ask, we do not guess.
Tiles are a separate trade page, but a bathroom is not finished with bare board. The quote says who is tiling.
Extract fans are part of stopping the mould coming back. We duct them outside, not into the loft to sweat on the joists.
Landlords want a bathroom a tenant can use on a date. We test the wastes and the fan before we call it done.

joinery.guide: Joinery and carpentry in a house is doors, skirting, architrave, stairs, stud walls, built-in wardrobes and decking. A joiner hangs a door so it latches, scribes skirting to a floor that is not flat, and builds a stud wall that is straight and ready for plasterboard. Fire doors are a particular job: the leaf, the closers, the gaps and the ironmongery have to match the reason the door is there. We do not plane a fire door to nothing and leave the closer off. Stair repairs deal with creaks, broken spindles and treads that have gone. Decking is set out, ventilated and fixed so it does not rock. The survey in {place} measures the openings and the floors before we cut anything.
paragraphs: Door hanging includes the lining if the old one is out of square. A new door in a twisted frame will always look wrong.
Skirting and architrave are scribed and mitred. We do not fill a 15 mm gap and call it a fit.
Stud walls are set out from the drawing, nogged for the plasterboard, and headed out for doors. Sockets are marked so the electrician is not guessing.
Built-in wardrobes are made to the alcove, including the ceiling that is not level. We agree shelves and hanging rail before we cut the board.
Stair repairs start with what is loose. We do not carpet over a moving tread and hope the creak goes.
Decking needs airflow underneath and a frame that is not sitting in soil. We set the falls so water leaves the house wall.
Internal doors in a rental are often slammed out of alignment. We rehang and adjust before we replace a door that is still sound.
Fire door fitting is explained in plain words: why the gaps matter and why the closer stays on.

flooring.guide: Flooring is laminate, LVT, engineered wood, vinyl, sanding, levelling, screed, and the joist or subfloor repairs that have to happen first. LVT needs a flat floor or the joints show every bump. Engineered wood moves with the room and needs the right acclimatising. Sanding an original floor is only worth it when the boards are thick enough. Screed and levelling compound are the unglamorous part that makes the finish look right. LVT is only as flat as the floor under it. Trowel ridges and old adhesive show through.
Engineered boards need a dry subfloor. We test. We do not stick wood to a damp slab and hope.
Floor sanding creates dust. We protect the stairs and we stop if the boards are too thin to sand again.
Vinyl in a bathroom or a kitchen needs a sound floor and sealed edges. It is not a cure for a rotten chipboard.
Screeding a room is a level and a dry-time. Furniture goes back when it is ready, not when the calendar says so.
Joist repair means lifting boards. We agree how much of the room is opened before we start.
Subfloor boards that are soft over a leaking pipe get replaced, and the leak is named rather than boarded over.

drainage.guide: Drainage work for a house is blocked drains, repairs, unblocking, CCTV surveys of the pipe (a camera in the drain, not a security camera), soakaways, relining, gullies and manholes. Emergency call-outs are for sewage where it should not be, or a drain that is flooding the garden in the rain. Relining suits a pipe that is cracked but still in line. A collapse is a dig. Soakaways are sized to the roof they serve and to the ground they sit in.

Gully repairs stop the path water going into the house. We reset or replace the pot and the pipe that leaves it.
Manhole repairs are frames, covers and benching. A rocking cover on a {place} pavement is a trip and a rattle.
Soakaways fail when they are too small or the ground is clay. We say if a soakaway is the wrong answer.
Relining avoids a dig across a drive when the pipe is a candidate for it. If it is collapsed, we excavate.
Emergency drainage is about stopping the damage today and booking the proper repair, not about a permanent patch at midnight.

damp.guide: Damp proofing for a house is finding why the wall is wet, then doing the thing that stops it. Rising damp, penetrating damp, condensation, a failed damp-proof course, tanking, basement waterproofing, cavity wall ties, mould, dry rot and woodworm are not one product. Condensation is often ventilation and heating, not an injection. Penetrating damp is a gutter, a pointing failure or a high garden. Rising damp is a specific diagnosis, not a label for every tide mark. We survey. An emergency visit is for water that is damaging the house today. Tanking a wet basement is a system, with the floor and the walls thought about together. We do not sell an injection cream for a leaking gutter.
paragraphs: A damp survey is the first job. It includes the outside: gutters, ground levels, pointing, and the cavity if we can see it.
Condensation mould in a bedroom is often the fan, the cold wall and the way the room is used. We treat the cause.
Penetrating damp shows after rain. We look at the elevation in the weather, not only at the stain indoors.
A damp-proof course injection is offered when the diagnosis supports it, not as a default.
Tanking and basement waterproofing are designed. A painted slurry on a wet wall with no drainage is not a system.
Cavity wall ties and debris in the cavity bridge damp. If that is the cause, an injection will not fix it.
Dry rot and woodworm need the timber opened up enough to see the extent. We do not spray a skirting and leave the joist.
Mould is cleaned after the moisture is dealt with. Painting over it is not the treatment.

insulation.guide: Insulation work is the loft, the cavity, internal wall insulation, external wall insulation and the underfloor quilt that stops a suspended floor being cold. It is also spray-foam removal, which is its own job because foam in a roof can hide rotten timber and can cause trouble when you sell. We do not pump a cavity that is full of rubble or already damp. A loft top-up is straightforward when the loft is empty and dangerous when it is full of boarding, tanks and old wiring. Internal insulation loses a little room and needs a careful vapour check. External insulation changes the look of the house and the details at windows and sills. We survey the loft and the walls before we name a thickness.

Internal wall insulation is detailed at the reveals and the floor so you do not create a cold strip and a mould line.
External wall insulation is a system with beads, sills and a render. It is not a slab stuck on and forgotten.
Underfloor insulation in a suspended floor needs access and a still-sound joist. We do not staple quilt to rotten timber.
Spray foam removal is slow and it is dusty. We inspect the rafters as the foam comes off and we tell you what we find.
Boarding a loft after insulating it needs a raised platform so the quilt is not crushed.
Electrics and downlights in an insulated ceiling are checked so a lamp is not buried in quilt.

topics.coving: Coving is the decorative moulding where the wall meets the ceiling. We run new lengths, mitre the corners and repair cracked or sagging cornice. A repair is let into the existing run so the profile matches. Filler smeared along a crack is not a coving repair.
topics.cornice-repair: Cornice repair matches the existing profile, cuts out the failed length and joins the new piece so the eye does not stop at the patch. We look at whether the ceiling behind it is moving before we stick anything back.
topics.artex: Artex and textured coatings are removed or skimmed over once we know what they are stuck to. The room is protected. You are left with a flat ceiling, not a half-scraped texture.
topics.grp-roofing: GRP, sometimes called fibreglass, is a resin flat-roof system laid over a dry, sound deck. Trims, outlets and the weather on the day all matter. We do not lay it on a soft or wet board.
topics.fibreglass-roofing: Fibreglass roofing is the same family as GRP: a laminated roof on a prepared deck, with the edge trims doing as much work as the flat. We survey the deck first.
topics.epdm-roofing: EPDM is a rubber sheet. The sheet is only as good as the outlet, the upstand and the deck it is stuck or laid on. We detail those rather than stretching a membrane over a ponding roof.
topics.rubber-roofing: Rubber roofing is a single-ply sheet, usually EPDM. Seams and the detail at the wall are the bits that leak if they are rushed. We look at the falls before we cover them up.
topics.security-lighting: Security lighting is an external light, often with a PIR, aimed at your path or drive. It is cabled from a proper point, not plugged into a trailing lead. We aim it so it does not blaze into the house next door.
topics.aov-motor: An AOV motor opens and closes the vent. When it fails, the vent sticks open, stuck shut, or moves and does not make the limit. We identify the motor from the label and test it from the panel after it is changed.
topics.aov-actuator: A window actuator is the device on the smoke vent or the stair window. Replacement includes the chain or spindle and a test that the window still shuts tight against the weather.
topics.smoke-damper: A smoke damper sits in the duct or the shaft and must move when the system asks it to. Testing is a look at the damper moving, not a tick on a sheet from the plant room doorway.
topics.louvre: A louvre vent is the bladed opening, often on a stair or a roof plant position. It has to open on the fire signal and close afterwards so the stair is not left open to the rain.
topics.eicr: An EICR is the electrical inspection of the installation. It is listed from £160. You get the report. Remedial work is a separate quote, not bundled in without being asked for.
topics.consumer-unit: A consumer unit upgrade replaces the fuse board, labels the circuits and is tested. We do not change a board to hide a fault we have not found.
topics.ev-charger: An EV charger needs a look at the supply, the earth and a safe route for the cable to the drive. The unit is commissioned and you are shown how it is isolated.
topics.wet-room: A wet room is a tanked floor with a fall to a drain, not tiles on a flat bathroom floor. The tanking and the waste are the job. The tiles come after.
topics.damp-proof: A damp-proof course is only part of a damp diagnosis. We check gutters, ground levels and the cavity before we talk about injection.
topics.loft-conversion: A loft conversion is stairs, structure, insulation and a room that has the headroom. We measure before we name it a dormer, a hip-to-gable or a Velux room.
topics.kitchen-fit: Kitchen fitting is units, worktops and services in the right order. Gas connections are carried out by Gas Safe registered engineers.
topics.flat-roof: A flat roof is the deck, the falls, the outlets and the covering, whether that covering is felt, GRP or EPDM. We do not cover a rotten deck.
topics.gutter: Guttering is the falls, the outlets and the brackets. A gutter full of silt or a downpipe that is disconnected will wet the wall no matter how new the tiles are.
topics.fascia: Fascias and soffits are the boards at the eaves. Replacement includes putting the gutter back on a straight line and keeping the roof ventilation.
topics.chimney: Chimney work is repointing, flaunching, pots, cowls, lead flashings and, where agreed, taking a stack down. Roof access is part of the quote.
topics.lead: Leadwork is flashings, valleys and soakers, dressed to the roof. Cement smeared where lead should be is not leadwork and we will not sell it as such.
topics.smoke-vent: A smoke vent is the opening that lets smoke out of the stair or the corridor. It has a panel, a power supply and a reason it opens. We test that chain, not just the hatch.
topics.smoke-control: Smoke control is the whole arrangement: vents, fans, dampers, shafts and the panel. Servicing records what moved and what did not.
topics.rewire: A rewire replaces the cables and the accessories that are in the scope, and it is tested. We agree how much of the house is open at once.
topics.downlight: Downlights are cut into the ceiling, wired, and fitted with the hoods or covers the ceiling needs. They are not buried in insulation without a plan.
topics.electric-shower: An electric shower needs a cable and a supply that can take the kilowatts, plus an isolator you can reach. If the old cable is the fault, we say so.
topics.fence: Fencing stands or falls on the posts. We set posts that will hold the panel or the close-board, and we hang gates on posts that are not already loose.
topics.block-paving: Block paving is a base, an edge and a fall. The blocks are the last layer. A soft base will sink however neat the pattern looks on day one.
topics.drainage: Drainage repairs start with where the water is going. A camera survey shows a crack or a root. We do not dig up a drive without that, unless the collapse is already obvious.
topics.extension: An extension is foundations, walls, a roof and an opening into the house you already live in. Drains and the neighbour's wall are checked before the dig.
topics.render: Rendering is the coat on the outside wall. We find out whether the old coat is hollow and whether the wall is damp before we put a new coat over it.
topics.plaster: Plastering makes a flat surface for decoration. We do not skim over damp or over plaster that is hollow and live.
